FEE ARM: CONTROL — flat 0.100 SKL per transaction at every height. A declared divergence: the chain charges no flat fee (ECONOMICS_SIM_PRODUCTION_REBASE.md §4).

Stage-2 archival burden trajectory (§12.1 checkpoint 1)
outputs = tx_volume x 2 (1in/2out normal traffic, drives tree depth); archival bytes = Σ tx_volume x archival_len(1in/2out @ depth) (9939..12627 B/tx shallow..deep);
n = shard_of(cumulative archival bytes), W = 3.0 MB/shard (SHT-Q2)
burden = n x W x storage($/B/yr, Kryder); base = 1e-11 $/B/yr; funding + clearance (A1) land next

Kryder band swept (DQ-2B):
  - 0%/yr (Kryder-stall / Arweave failure face; BINDING)
  - 10%/yr (post-2010s $/GB slowdown)
  - 25%/yr (long-run historical $/GB decline)

A4 (W9) stuffer cost — max-archival-bytes-per-fee shape (8-in/1-out, searched over every
builder-legal shape), min weight-fee @ 300 atomic/byte, W = 3.0 MB/shard:
Monero-replication anchor (DQ-2C): the March-2024 spam bought ~3.08 GB / 23 days
for ~61.5 XMR — that byte volume is ~1026 Shekyl shards' worth of archival good.
Shape is max-archival-per-fee geometry (inputs carry the PQC auth + FCMP share the
operand counts; outputs carry unprunable prefix it does not), NOT decoy poisoning
(FCMP++ has no rings). 'sustained' prices the cheapest output-conserving
producer/consumer cycle — what a campaign that must mint its own inputs pays.
chain n(shards) depth        shape   fee/tx (SKL)  tx/shard   cost/shard (SKL)      sustained (SKL)
1                   1   8-in/1-out       0.016304        57             0.9294               1.0262
100000              5   8-in/1-out       0.017936        52             0.9327               1.0045
500000              5   8-in/1-out       0.017936        52             0.9327               1.0045
2250000             6   8-in/1-out       0.018109        52             0.9417               0.9992
10000000            6   8-in/1-out       0.018109        52             0.9417               0.9992
  -> cost/shard is depth-FLAT to within a few percent (the FCMP proof grows with
depth, but it is archival good the stuffer is buying, so only the archival/weight
ratio moves): one-shot drifts UP ~1%, sustained DOWN ~3%. The leaf era's
'cheapest early' is gone with its unit. The A4 ROI gate below weighs the one-shot
(binding, attacker-favouring) cost against the escalation Delta-pool a stuffing
staker captures: a survivor of A1 must ALSO price the stuffer out.

A1 — burden clearance (§12.2, F-G): min budget / (bond-opp-cost + storage) ratio.
budget = emission_leg + fee_burn x share(n) [SKL]; binding burden = bond_floor 0.75 x R6 x n x rate.
>=1.0 keeps the staker whole every sustained year. Columns = opp-cost rate [0.02, 0.05, 0.1] (10% binding).
Storage is a minor add-on (F-G: ~100x smaller); the binding term is PRICE-INDEPENDENT (SKL vs SKL).
Knee band [500000, 2250000, 10000000] closed shards; the shipped middle is 6.75 TB of archival at W = 3000000 B/shard.

earning its keep. A4/A5 then drop any winner that fails W9/W10.
'R sustained' = R6 x ratio: the replica count the budget would carry at
10% (both burden terms are linear in R), so a fail reads as a number.
The 10%/yr binding rate is EXOGENOUS: SKL bonded for decades in a settled
chain at ~15 tx/block is where that assumption is strongest and least
grounded; the band is kept, the choice of binding member is the owner's.
  -> VERDICT @10%: D2 case (best clears, flat does not): none; cleared by NO
candidate in the band: high_history_low_activity. Byte-keyed, n counts ~10 KB of archival per
transaction, not one 128-B leaf per output, so the §6.2 coupled bond per unit
of traffic is ~40x the leaf-era figure — a scenario the leaf-era sweep cleared
can fail here on the bond term alone, with no change to the escalation.
  -> NO DISCRIMINATING SCENARIO AT THIS HORIZON: across the whole set, every
scenario either clears flat or clears for no candidate — within its own
sim_years the escalation does no work the flat share does not. That is a
statement about the horizon, not the lever: A1-T below runs the same
scenarios to 60 y, where the staker emission leg has decayed under the bond
burden and the region (flat fails, best clears) opens at the low rates
(ARCHIVAL_WORK_PRECISION_AND_ESCALATION.md §12.13–§12.14).

A1-T — ONSET of A1 failure (§12.14): every scenario run to 60 y; the min hides WHEN.
'xover' = first year the staker EMISSION leg alone < bond opp cost @10% (end of the
era emission carries). 'onset' = first sustained year budget/burden < 1 (shipped burn
x share; '*' = a later year clears again; 'never' = clears to 60 y). Schedules are
the scenarios' own closures past their horizons: constant, cyclic, or growing —
sustained_growth's 20%/yr to 60 y is unphysical (block weight caps it, and by ~y38
its fee burn has destroyed the circulating supply, so burn_pct -> 0 and the fee
leg with it) and is read for shape only.

  -> FEE HORIZON (closed form, constant traffic V): the fee leg clears a corpus no
deeper than H = fee x base x share x W / (bond x R x rate x bytes/tx) traffic-years.
fee 0.100 SKL/tx, W 3000000 B, bond 0.75 SKL x R6, 12627 archival B/tx (1in/2out,
deep). V cancels between fees and corpus; for a share of ALL fees H is therefore
traffic-independent. For a share of the BURN, base = burn_pct rises as sqrt(V)
(calc_burn_pct, supply emitted) until burn_cap binds at V = 162 tx/block, so H
rises with traffic up to the cap (1.8x the baseline figure) and is flat above:
       burn x flat 25%  scen. 9 tail (  15 tx/blk, burn_pct 0.27)  H = 18y @2%, 7y @5%, 4y @10%
       burn x flat 25%  baseline     (  50 tx/blk, burn_pct 0.50)  H = 33y @2%, 13y @5%, 7y @10%
       burn x flat 25%  at burn_cap  ( 162 tx/blk, burn_pct 0.90)  H = 59y @2%, 24y @5%, 12y @10%
       burn x 100%      scen. 9 tail (  15 tx/blk, burn_pct 0.27)  H = 72y @2%, 29y @5%, 14y @10%
       burn x 100%      baseline     (  50 tx/blk, burn_pct 0.50)  H = 132y @2%, 53y @5%, 26y @10%
       burn x 100%      at burn_cap  ( 162 tx/blk, burn_pct 0.90)  H = 238y @2%, 95y @5%, 48y @10%
       ALL fees x 100%  any V        ( any tx/blk, base 1.00)  H = 264y @2%, 106y @5%, 53y @10%
     Corpus older than H is unfunded by fees, and past the cap no amount of traffic
moves H; a busier chain crosses the same line later only because its corpus is
younger. No FLOW — fee share, burn share, or the constant tail — funds a
fixed-per-shard bond held forever on a corpus that grows forever; the operand to
question is the bond (§12.14 Ruling: bond sizing vs per-shard reward).

genesis-frozen or ceremony-gated number. 'ALL fees' reaches into the miner's income —
the fee-era PoW security budget; that trade needs its own wargame, not a parameter.
'tail floor p%' = staker leg floored at p% of ALL block emission, non-decaying (at the
tail: p% of 157680 SKL/yr). 'decay' re-pins shekyl_staker_emission_decay.

(0.75 SKL locked per 3000000 B forever, R = 6): what it is FOR decides its size.

A3 — budget stranding (§12.2): fraction of budget(E) that NEVER MINTS.
budget is a minting ENTITLEMENT — unclaimed past MAX_CLAIM_AGE_W=26 is "supply
never created" (ARCHIVAL_BUDGET_SCHEDULE §4). A class claims iff its reward
covers one claim tx (0.003778..0.004585 SKL early..late @ the 300 atomic/byte
floor, via the production predictor at each year's tree depth). PRE-D1 vs
POST-D1 scoring = the §1 Stage-0 coupling claim, measured: pre-D1 zeroes bulk
holders past the co-holder cliff (r_market > g_milli ≈ 1000), and a
structural-zero cohort's slice never mints.
archivers    mean_r        n  pre strand pre zero%  post strand post zero% post noclm%
2000             10    51313       0.00%      0.0%        0.00%      0.0%       0.0%  early
20000           109    51313       0.00%      0.0%        0.00%      0.0%       0.0%  early
60000           327    51313       0.00%      0.0%        0.00%      0.0%       0.0%  early
2000              1   313828       0.00%      0.0%        0.00%      0.0%       0.0%  mid
20000            17   313828       0.00%      0.0%        0.00%      0.0%       0.0%  mid
60000            53   313828       0.00%      0.0%        0.00%      0.0%       0.0%  mid
2000              1   523841       0.00%      0.0%        0.00%      0.0%       0.0%  late
20000            10   523841       0.00%      0.0%        0.00%      0.0%       0.0%  late
60000            32   523841       0.00%      0.0%        0.00%      0.0%       0.0%  late
  -> Read: the §1 Stage-0 claim is CONFIRMED, and stronger than stated — where
mean_r crosses the co-holder cliff (~1000) pre-D1 strands 100% of budget,
not 'partly': EVERY class floors to zero, so the whole epoch's entitlement is
supply-never-created. Replication = archivers x holdings / n, so this is an
EARLY-CHAIN regime (few shards, many holders) the corpus grows out of — and one a
large archiver population re-enters at any n. D2-without-D1 would have escalated
a pool that evaporates ENTIRELY in exactly the bootstrap window that most needs
archivers paid.
RESIDUAL = a QUANTIZATION FLOOR, not a remaining defect: D1 does not abolish
structural zeros, it SCALES the cliff with holdings to r > ~1000 x shards_held
(the micro sum must reach one milli). Unreachable for a bulk holder (4096 shards
⇒ r > 4M); a 16-shard hobbyist still zeroes at r > ~16k — the 70% column above.
Sub-milli work is UNREPRESENTABLE under the frozen WORK_MILLI_SCALE, so the
honest name is a MINIMUM VIABLE HOLDING THRESHOLD, not a bug: eliminating it
would mean changing a frozen constant. The archiver's levers are holdings size
and replication depth. It is the third force in D3's holdings-size triangle.
Joint with A1: stranded budget is not burden-clearing.

OQ-1 (D3 round §12.8) — provisional A2 distribution probe: is deleting the
curve_milli plateau DISTRIBUTION-NEUTRAL in equilibrium? Hypothesis:
distribution(cap-deleted) == distribution(cap-kept + rational splitting).
Classes = DQ-2H [(700, 16), (250, 256), (50, 4096)] (per-mille, shards). Split bonds = 4 shards.
All three regimes scored through the PRODUCTION chain, so the split-dodge
meets the quantization floor rather than being assumed free.
r_market        cap-kept-NAIVE shares    cap-kept-RATIONAL shares          cap-DELETED shares  |Δ| rat-del
6                   0.437/0.469/0.094           0.040/0.229/0.731           0.040/0.229/0.731     0.0000
100                 0.097/0.556/0.347           0.040/0.229/0.731           0.040/0.229/0.731     0.0000
5000                0.038/0.228/0.734           0.038/0.228/0.734           0.038/0.228/0.734     0.0000
100000              0.000/0.200/0.800           0.000/0.200/0.800           0.000/0.200/0.800     0.0000

  naive-fraction sweep at r=6 (divergence of mixed play from cap-DELETED):
    f=0.0:0.0000  0.2:0.0143  0.4:0.0367  0.6:0.0770  0.8:0.1709  1.0:0.6377  
  -> Read: |Δ| rat-del ≈ 0 at EVERY r CONFIRMS OQ-1 — under best-response play the
plateau distributes exactly as its own deletion would, so G-2's distributional
counter-consideration is empirically DISCHARGED: deletion is distribution-neutral
in equilibrium. It holds by two different routes, which is what makes it robust:
at shallow r the actor SPLITS and escapes the cap; at deep r splitting would
quantize to zero so the actor does NOT split — and there the cap does not bind
anyway (work sits below the knee), so unsplit == deleted. Either way the plateau
is inert against an optimizing actor.
The NAIVE column is the plateau's only observable effect: it redistributes FROM
the large class TO smalls, but strictly over the naive fraction — it taxes those
who do not optimize. That is R1's distortion wearing a defense's name.
Caveat for R3: the deep-r zeros in the SplitDodge regime are why min_holding must
be sized against quantization — the dodge is self-limiting, not unconditional.

OQ-2 (D3 round §12.8) — sizing the R3 minimum-holding admission floor.
Boundary (production chain, not a closed form): min_holding(r) = least h whose
h x scarcity_micro(r) reaches one milli ≈ ceil(r/1000) — the mirror of the
r > ~1000 x shards_held cliff. Purpose: make guaranteed-zero bonds
UNREPRESENTABLE rather than merely unprofitable (they lock capital into a
position the frozen scale cannot pay). Safety multiple = 2x.
archivers          n    mean_r   min_viable_h split-loss@4096
2000           51313        10              1              0
20000          51313       109              1            712
60000          51313       327              1            237
2000          261325         2              1              0
20000         261325        21              1           2535
60000         261325        64              1           2560
2000          523841         1              1              0
20000         523841        10              1              0
60000         523841        32              1           1024
  -> RECOMMENDED provisional min_holding = 2 shards (2x the worst swept
boundary). Composes with the wire cap: true (must sit strictly below
MAX_HOLDINGS_SHARDS = 4096). Genesis-provisional NUMBER under a frozen SHAPE
(bond_duration posture): re-pin at testnet against MEASURED replication, with a
named reopen — r is a forecast, and under-sizing is the costly direction
(an under-sized floor admits the very zero-scoring bonds R3 exists to refuse).
CLUSTERING: none expected. Under R2 (plateau deleted) credited work is LINEAR,
so bond count does not change total credit — the splitting incentive that
motivated D3 is gone. The residual pressure runs the other way: each bond
floors independently, so splitting discards sub-milli remainders (the
split-loss column). Consolidation is weakly preferred; nobody is pushed to sit
at exactly the floor.

OQ-4 (D3 round §12.8) — A4 gate under PLATEAU DELETION (scenario baseline_steady_stat, n=523841,
steepest candidate, Δn=10000, H=10y). Prediction: the capped column vanishes and
the realistic-end numbers become the only numbers.
honest regime                       ROI     fee x -> 1
kept, small bonds (h=4)          0.0104            0.0
kept, capped (h=512)             0.0757            0.0
DELETED (h irrelevant)           0.0104            0.0
  -> Read: deletion reproduces the small-bond row exactly — under R2 there is no
cap to dodge, so the honest-holdings axis stops mattering and A4 has ONE number
per regime instead of a naive/rational spread. fee_mult_to_close is unchanged
from the realistic end, so reopen (c)'s sizing evidence SURVIVES deletion
(it was sized there already). The capped row is what deletion removes: a
penalty that fell on non-optimizing honest archivers and doubled the stuffer's
relative capture.

A2 — distributional shift (W6, §12.2): does D1 bringing ex-zero bulk holders
into Σwork dilute SCARCE holders below their marginal cost? Population =
DQ-2H size classes x holding-scarcity bands [(100, 2), (600, 6), (200, 50), (100, 3000)] (per-mille, r). The last
band sits PAST the co-holder cliff — a structural zero pre-D1, paid post-D1,
which is the whole mechanism. Regime = PLATEAU DELETED (D3/R2), the sole live
regime: no curve, so credited work IS work and there is no naive/rational axis.
Margin = reward - (bond opp cost @ 10% + storage), SKL/epoch, at baseline_steady_st n=523841.

A6 — swing / band width (§12.2): the empirical check on §6.0's STRUCTURAL claim
that the operand cannot swing (monotone + slow + no controller ⇒ W8 armed by
operand). Binding input is a W9 FLOOD, not organic growth — a stuffer buying
archival bytes at the block-weight ceiling is the fastest n can physically move.
Ceiling: 300000 B/block floor x4 surge = 1200000 B, reached after
~102 blocks of sustained flood (1.0% of an epoch); epoch = 10000 blocks;
reorg reach = 720 blocks. Curve = steepest candidate (asymptote 90%,
knee 10000000) — a cliff would surface there first.
        n     Δn/epoch   Δshare/epoch   Δshare %pts/ep %pts/ep w/penalty reorg Δshare%pt
        0         3865            502          0.0502%           0.1005%         0.0036%
   100000         3877            504          0.0504%           0.1008%         0.0036%
   500000         3877            504          0.0504%           0.1008%         0.0036%
  2250000         3808            495          0.0495%           0.0992%         0.0035%
 10000000         3808              0          0.0000%           0.0000%         0.0000%
  -> Read: 'Δshare %pts/ep' is the MAXIMUM the staker share can move in one
settlement epoch when an adversary floods at the surge ceiling for the whole
epoch — the worst case for §6.0's no-swing claim. Worst observed: 0.0504 points.
The reorg column bounds the only DOWN-swing that exists (monotonicity holds in
the canonical chain; a reorg can re-open at most 720 blocks' worth).
VERDICT: no measurable adversarial slew.
  -> §6.0/§6.1 SEPARATED, because they are different claims:
(a) CLIFF (structural, §6.1's actual requirement) — NOT present. The share is
monotone and a single shard never moves it discontinuously; the family's
`no_cliff_bounded_slope` test pins that, and the reorg column shows the only
down-swing reaches 0.0036 points. W8 stands armed BY OPERAND.
(b) ADVERSARIAL SLEW RATE (economic) — 0.0504 pts/epoch penalty-free, 0.1008
pts/epoch if the flooder also compensates the miner penalty (the legal 2x
limit). MEASURED against blockchain.cpp's ArticMine algorithm, not derived —
the ceiling a flood can force at maximum effort. A rate, not a cliff,
and it is bounded, monotone and one-directional — but it is NOT invisible,
which is the honest correction to a purely structural reading of §6.0.
It is also PRICED, and the legal-limit price is dominated by a term that is
NOT the fees: ~7174 SKL/epoch in stuffing fees at the A4 rate, PLUS
~10240000 SKL/epoch of miner-reward penalty compensation — at B = 2M the
production penalty formula (get_block_reward) pays the miner EXACTLY ZERO,
so the flooder must fund the whole block reward, every block, or no rational
miner includes the flood. Measured, not derived. A4 already gates whether
such a flood pays (it does not, once the reopen-(c) fee-floor lands). So the swing lever exists physically and is
closed ECONOMICALLY, not structurally — Stage 3 should freeze the shape
knowing that, rather than on the stronger claim that no lever exists.

A4 — W9 output-stuffing ROI (§12.2, DQ-2C): SERVED-WORK capture (the D2 pool

Flat-25 has no share lever ⇒ 0. Attacker-favouring: min opp-rate 0.02, storage
omitted, age-0. PASS iff realistic-end (hHold=4) ROI < 1 everywhere.

A4 decomposition — realistic-end (hHold=4) worst config per scenario. Size the
remedy against the DOMINANT term, not the ratio (§12.2, per the D-2 retraction):
revenue = Δpool-flow x capture; cost = fees + coupled bond. 'prem' = capture /
proportional (first-mover premium); 'fee×→1' = the per-output fee multiplier that
would drive ROI to 1 in THIS regime; 'ROI(resp)' = ROI once honest replicas answer
(r:1→6 after 2y lag; first-order, NOT gating).

  -> Read: prem≈1.0 at the realistic end ⇒ NO concentration premium — the attack is
pure fee-flow-volume leverage (cheap stuffing unlocks a large Δpool; the attacker
takes only their proportional slice, but the pool dwarfs the stuffing cost). The
fee-RATE cancels in fee×→1, so its 0.8→2.0x spread is volume/share-slope
variation: one fee-floor sized for the worst regime over-charges benign traffic
~3x in the mildest — the remedy's real cost. Denominate it in WEIGHT (a
virtual-weight surcharge rides the fee market over time; an atomic constant rots)
— but weight alone can't erase the cross-regime spread. The D3 dodge is load-bearing
at the CAPPED-honest end (prem>1, ROI several x higher); its undodgeable-cap fix
prices concentration in bonded capital THERE. So the pair: fee-floor for the
fee-flow regime, D3 for the capped one.

A5 — W10 proxy free-rider margin (§12.2/§11.1): GATE2-conformant cheap opening
(128-B leaf + shallow ~6784-B segment co-path; fetch-on-demand IS service, NOT
durability). margin/epoch = proxy(re-fetch + L14 slash exposure) − honest storage.
PASS iff margin > 0. L14 rides the CORRECTED m-of-n slash (m=11/n=13: a single
missed re-fetch is ABSORBED — deterrent is WEAKER than single-strike).

  -> W10 gate: FAILS at the current grace window (margin@q=0 < 0 — re-fetch is ~KB
vs 12.3 GB held, so honest holding is the DEARER strategy: the proxy free-rides).
'q*' = the per-epoch re-fetch-FAILURE rate the gate-4 grace window must force for
the m-of-n slash exposure to flip the margin positive — i.e. how tight grace must

D2 helps here — but the current hours-long grace gives q≈0, so it does not bind.
§11.1 disposition (NOT a D2 redesign): tighten gate-4 grace to force q ≥ q*, OR
accelerate the PoRep reopen (q→1: re-fetch cannot substitute for sealed possession
— the whole-shard/actual-possession test, a NAMED non-genesis path).

TJ-4/TJ-7 — the two inequalities the (m,n) re-pin needs (m=11/n=13).
BOND_FLOOR = 0.750 SKL per shard. Deterministic no-slash fraction 0.2308
bounds a PLACING adversary only; under an unchooseable draw absorption is
deferred, not prevented, so the cycle question stays live across the range.
OPERAND DIRECTION (labelled at the number): A5 uses the scenario-family MAX
per-shard pool because there a larger forfeit is a STRONGER deterrent, so
max is conservative. For TJ-4/TJ-7 it runs the OTHER WAY -- a larger reward
makes the slash/Reinstate cycle and the dilution MORE profitable -- so max is
the ALARM-RAISING end. Tables below run the MEDIAN (0.1691 SKL/shard/epoch);
the max (442.0433) is reported as the bound beneath each.
  TJ-4 CORRECTION (reward path, verified): a ZERO-service P earns NOTHING
(shard_work_micro returns 0 without serve credit; reward pays on credited
work), so the m-1 unslashable epochs are free of SLASH, not free MONEY.
The inequality is only non-trivial when the pair is being credited, i.e.
at attestation fraction f > 0 — so the derived quantity is a break-even f.
Earnings assume sole credited holder (r = 1) — attacker-favourable.
  FRICTION (derived, not assumed). What a Reinstate IS (gate-4 SS 3.4/P2B-9):
REINSTATEMENT, NOT RE-ENTRY — the slash burns one FLOOR and removes the
shard atomically, so Reinstate credit is owed for growth only (zero for the
common standing-only form); the slash-EMPTIED single-shard cycle pair
must therefore re-add its shard at FLOOR. Reinstate closes the bad interval
at end_exclusive = E_reinstate + 1, so exclusion runs the slash epoch
THROUGH the reinstate epoch inclusive — structural floor 2 epochs of
FORGONE EARNINGS: the slash for epoch e folds only past H_close(e) +
SLASH_GRACE_EPOCHS·SEB (one epoch of slash grace), writing the
interval RETROACTIVELY at start = e, so the earliest reachable reinstate
is in epoch e+2 and epochs e+1..=e+2 are voided (epoch e is the
absorbing miss — already unpaid; claim order enforces the retro void:
e+1 claims open only at e+3, after the fold). The connect's validation
admits a same-epoch close — probed, and MORE permissive than
reachability allows: slack, not a route. Forgone earnings are priced at the
CREDITED rate f*R, not full R (full-R overstates the deterrent 1/f-fold).
Zeroing this term was mislabelled 'attacker-favourable' in the first cut
— the attacker-favourable end is this floor, not zero. LABELLED
APPROXIMATION (attacker-favourable): the re-added shard takes add_epoch =
E_reinstate (Pin 7), so any age weighting of reward restarts each cycle;
using the steady-state per-shard pool as R OVERSTATES cycle earnings,
making every break-even below a LOWER BOUND. Table and break-evens run
downtime = 2.

  -> TJ-4 break-even f = 0.2311 (downtime at the structural floor of
2 epochs; a cooldown only raises it — curve below). Below it the
burned bond is not covered and the window is NOT a subscription fee;
above it the cycle pays and attestation-resistance is what must carry
the deterrent.
NOTE: 0.2308 is the DETERMINISTIC no-slash fraction, which bounds an
adversary that can PLACE its passing epochs. Under SS 8.2's unchooseable
draw the cartel cannot place them, so absorption still occurs above it
— deferred, not prevented.
     bound at the MAX operand (442.0433 SKL/shard/epoch): break-even f = 0.0002.
Both ends of the family are reported so the verdict is a RANGE, not a
point chosen by which operand happened to be at hand.
  -> WHY it breaks even so low: the burned bond is worth 4.43 EPOCHS of the
per-shard reward it secures (0.750 SKL vs 0.1691 SKL/epoch at the median).
A slash that costs a fraction of one epoch's earnings is not a penalty,
which is TJ-4's BOND_FLOOR coupling made quantitative: the (m,n) re-pin
cannot carry attestation-resistance while the collateral it forfeits is
this cheap relative to the flow. Raising m/lowering n does not fix a
floor problem.

  REMEDY CURVE — break-even f vs a hypothetical POST-SLASH COOLDOWN c
(Reinstate not admitted until c epochs after the slash; excluded span =
c + 2). f is the cartel's share of the UNCHOOSEABLE witness draw — its
hashrate share — so each row reads 'the cycle pays only above this
fraction of network hashrate'. 'none' = the cycle never pays anywhere
absorption is measurable within the horizon.
cooldown     ~weeks   break-even f (med)   break-even f (max)
0               0.0               0.2311               0.0002
1               2.0               0.2361               0.0002
2               4.0               0.2411               0.0003
4               7.9               0.2507               0.0003
8              15.8               0.2688               0.0017
16             31.7               0.2997               0.1988
32             63.3               0.3441               0.3045
64            126.6               0.3957               0.3806
  -> READING THE CURVE (the false dichotomy dissolved): BOND_FLOOR is
f-INDEPENDENT, so it bounds the low-f attacker; the downtime term d*f*R
SCALES with f, so it does its work at high f. 'Floor problem vs cooldown
problem' names two regimes, not two rival remedies — and the low-f regime
is what the structural floor alone leaves unpriced. HONEST LIMIT: no
finite cooldown makes the cycle unprofitable at literally every f;
E[epochs] grows without bound toward the measurable ceiling, so a cartel
with enough of the draw outlasts any fixed exclusion. What a cooldown
does is push break-even INTO the hashrate-expensive regime, where f
itself is the deterrent. REMEDY STAKES: raising BOND_FLOOR is linear in
shard count (a 4096-shard honest archiver already posts 3072 SKL) and
taxes exactly the mid-size participants distribution depends on; a
post-slash cooldown costs nothing to anyone who is not slashed and
scales with the offense. The curve is an INPUT to the (m,n) re-pin
sweep, not a verdict — TJ-8's briefing constraint carries unchanged.
  -> ENFORCEMENT POINT (briefing constraint, TJ-8 shape): the x-axis is
EXCLUSION EPOCHS PER CYCLE, however enforced. A Reinstate-only cooldown is
the WEAKEST enforcement: personas are free (G-1) and sybil-per-shard is
capital-bounded only (TJ-7), so a cartel abandons the slashed record and
bonds a FRESH pair on the same shard — same burned bond, no cooldown
served. A CREDIT-ONSET delay (minimum observation count — TJ-4's
original finding) yields the same per-cycle exclusion term on EVERY
route, fresh or reinstated; this curve prices both mechanisms
identically, so briefing it as 'add a Reinstate cooldown' would claim
resistance the record-scoped gate cannot carry.
THE KNEE: E[epochs] >= m always (a slash needs m misses), so up to
c + 2 = m = 11 the reward decides; past it break-even is FLOORED at
the f where E[epochs] = c + 2 REGARDLESS of reward — the cycle is
excluded longer than it can possibly earn — which is why the median and
max columns converge once c + 2 > 11.

  TJ-7 sybil-per-shard: pool is CONSERVED (C*g/r over r credited bonds),
so N sybils vs h honest take N/(N+h)*g, NOT N*g — dilution, not
multiplication. Tables report MARGINAL gain over one bond
([N/(N+h) - 1/(1+h)]*g), which saturates at h/(1+h)*g, not at g.
Cost is linear in N. Break-even = the ANNUAL return on locked capital
below which it pays. Same operand-direction rule as TJ-4: median first,
max as the alarm-raising bound.
  TJ-7 at MEDIAN pool g = 0.1691 SKL/epoch (sole credited holder; pool is

(§11.4): a single operator behind N personas is NOT a mechanism concern —

participation distribution is a tacit-vote outcome. This table prices
DILUTION OF HONEST CO-HOLDERS, which is a reward-fairness question, not a
storage-accounting one.

(m,n) FEASIBILITY — region, not optimum (wide-guardrails: a shipped
constant moves only if the region EXCLUDES it).
Inputs: lambda_target=3.000 reads/pair/epoch; OPERATIVE evaluation at
DELIVERED lambda=1.500 (projection 40000 pairs; k_cap binds past
20000 pairs, so target and delivered coincide only below that knee);
p_attempt=0.300 (STAND-IN: measured 2026-07-30 with NO PoW and NO
flood -- does not transfer to the SP-T3 operating point; the rig re-run
gates the real value), r=1, fabrication_intensity=1.00 (1.00 =
every gap epoch poisoned).
  OBSERVATION UNIT (correction the miss-fact ruling forces): an epoch's
reads collapse to ONE observation (any pass dominates), so observations
arrive at 1.0000/epoch -- NOT lambda_eff/epoch. A 13-observation window
spans ~13.0 epochs, so detection latency does NOT collapse and the
within-epoch independence worry does not arise (draws stay one per epoch,
weeks apart). What lambda_eff buys instead: pass-dominance COMPOUNDS the
transport term across an epoch's reads -- (p^r)^j for j reads, not p^r --
so coverage and retry depth are SUBSTITUTES on that term, and coverage's
version has better independence (j miners, j circuits vs r retries on one).
  TERMS: gap (poisonable) = e^-lambda = 0.2231; read-failure p^r = 0.3000;
per-epoch missed = 0.349938; per-OBSERVATION miss q = 0.349938.
Bond life 131 epochs; union-bound ceiling = 131 observations
(<= 1 obs/epoch; E[obs] = bond_life * rate = 131.0).
  SHIPPED PIN (11 of 13): false-slash/pair over bond life = 4.133e-2;
at MAX_HOLDINGS (4096 pairs) = 1.000e0 vs target 1.0e-3 per ARCHIVER --
EXCEEDS, margin 1.0e-3x on the operator axis; free-ride fraction =
0.769 (W16 bound 0.800); region membership = OUTSIDE.
  EXPOSURE FRAMING — RULED: P(any pair slashed) is the operative frame,
and the reason is mechanical rather than a risk preference. A slash
opens a bad interval on the RECORD (bad_intervals are record-scoped, not
per-shard), which excludes the whole record from r_market via
good_through and blocks HoldingsUpdate until Reinstate. One pair slashed is
therefore a whole-portfolio disruption plus a burn -- the harm is
record-scoped, so the probability must be too. At the shipped pin,
P(any of 4096 pairs) = 1.000e0; EXPECTED pairs lost = 1.693e2 (~126.9592
SKL of 3072 posted) is recorded only to show the ~4096x framing gap the
ruling closes -- it prices the burn while ignoring the exclusion, which
is the larger harm.
  SENSITIVITY — does the shipped (11,13) clear the floor? Evaluated at
the TARGETED fabrication intensity (F-1): sets are miner-chosen, so an
adversary attacking one victim does NOT spray -- it puts the victim in
its k slots in every block it wins, and poisoning an epoch needs ONE won
block, so phi = 1-(1-f)^SEB saturates at ~1 by f = 1e-3. The ambient
(no-victim) column 1-e^-(f*lambda) is shown only as the contrast; the
floor must be read against the targeted one. Rows are evaluated at the
operative delivered coverage; r stays unpinned pending the PoW-enabled
rig re-run.
